title: Free JEE DPP Mathematics: The Daily Practice Routine That Builds Speed (+ Quiz)
meta_title: Free JEE DPP Mathematics: Daily Practice Routine + Quiz
meta_desc: Build a free JEE DPP mathematics routine for speed: a weekly plan across every unit, an error log habit and a 20-question quiz. Try it now.
excerpt: A free JEE DPP mathematics guide: how to build a daily practice routine across every unit, plus a 20-question mixed quiz to test yourself.
author: Sachin Sharma
content:
Here is a pattern I see often. An aspirant knows the theory, but a limit that should take ninety seconds eats six minutes. So the marks leak on speed, not on ideas. A free JEE DPP mathematics habit closes that gap. It means a short, mixed set of daily practice problems. You solve them cold, every day, across the whole syllabus. This guide gives the routine, plus a quiz to test yourself.

What a DPP is

A DPP is a small daily sheet, usually eight to fifteen questions. The key word is mixed. It gives one algebra item, then one calculus item, then one coordinate item. So you must first name the topic before you solve it. That is the exact skill the real paper rewards.

Why daily beats a marathon

Two ideas explain the edge. First, spaced retrieval makes each method stick harder. So ten problems a day beat one long Sunday grind. Second, interleaving forces a fresh choice of tool every time. That feels harder, but it transfers to the exam. In fact, blocked practice feels smooth yet fades fast.

Your weekly free JEE DPP mathematics plan

  • Monday, algebra, so quadratics and sequences stay warm.
  • Tuesday, calculus, and a mix of limits and integrals.
  • Wednesday, coordinate geometry, then lines and conics.
  • Thursday, trigonometry, and identities plus equations.
  • Friday, vectors and 3D, so dot and cross products stay sharp.
  • Saturday, one timed mixed set, because exams feel mixed.
  • Sunday, review, and redo only the ones you missed.

Keep an error log

The Sunday step is the one people skip. So keep an error log, one line per wrong answer. Write the topic, and why you missed it. Some slips are concept gaps, but many are plain sign errors. After three weeks, the log turns into a map of weak spots.

Try the free mixed quiz

First find your weakest unit. The quiz below holds 20 mixed MCQs from across the syllabus. So it spans algebra, calculus, coordinate geometry and more. Answer each one, then read every reason you missed. Aim for 15 out of 20.

Practise with ready-made papers

Do you want full mixed sets already built? The JEE Maths 30 Practice Papers e-book sequences the difficulty and adds worked solutions, all for Rs 79. You can also browse every title on the JEE Mathematics e-book shelf. For free theory first, use the JEE Maths course at vidaara.org. So pair a free JEE DPP mathematics routine with these papers, and your speed climbs.

quiz.title: JEE Maths Mixed DPP Quiz
quiz.intro: Twenty JEE Main-level questions spread across the whole maths syllabus. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: (2 + i)(3 + 2i) equals:
The sum of an infinite GP is 4 and its first term is 2; the common ratio is:
The constant term in the expansion of (1 + x)ⁿ (1 + 1/x)ⁿ is:
questions.explanation: The product equals (1 + x)²ⁿ/xⁿ. The constant term is the coefficient of xⁿ in (1 + x)²ⁿ, which is ²ⁿCₙ.

questions.q: The area of the triangle formed by the axes and the line 3x + 4y = 12 is:
questions.explanation: The intercepts are 4 and 3. Area = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 sq units.

questions.q: The parabola x² = 4ay passes through (2, 1); its latus rectum length is:
questions.explanation: Put (2, 1): 4 = 4a, so a = 1. The latus rectum is 4a = 4 units.

questions.q: For x²/16 − y²/9 = 1, the transverse and conjugate axes are:
questions.explanation: Here 2a = 8 and 2b = 6, so the axes are 8 and 6.

questions.q: The derivative of x logₑ x is:
questions.explanation: By the product rule, logₑ x + x·(1/x) = 1 + logₑ x.

questions.q: The function f(x) = 2x³ − 3x² − 36x + 7 is strictly decreasing in:
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 6(x − 3)(x + 2). It is negative on (−2, 3), so f decreases there.

questions.q: The area bounded by y = x², the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = 2 is:
questions.explanation: Area = ∫₁² x² dx = 8/3 − 1/3 = 7/3 sq units.

questions.q: The general solution of dy/dx = 1/(1 + x²) is:
questions.explanation: Integrate 1/(1 + x²) to get tan⁻¹x + C.

questions.q: The standard deviation of the first 10 natural numbers is about:
questions.explanation: Variance = (n² − 1)/12 = 99/12 = 8.25. So the standard deviation is √8.25 ≈ 2.87.

questions.q: tan⁻¹(1/2) + tan⁻¹(1/3) equals:
questions.explanation: The product 1/6 is below 1, so the sum is tan⁻¹((1/2 + 1/3)/(1 − 1/6)) = tan⁻¹1 = π/4.

questions.q: In a triangle with sides 3, 5 and 7, the greatest angle is:
questions.explanation: The greatest angle faces side 7. cos C = (9 + 25 − 49)/(2·3·5) = −1/2, so C = 120°.

questions.q: The distance of the point P(−4, 3, 5) from the origin is:
The negation of 'All equilateral triangles are isosceles' is:
options: All equilateral triangles are not isosceles.
There exists an equilateral triangle that is not isosceles.
There exists an isosceles triangle that is not equilateral.
questions.explanation: The negation of 'for all x, P(x)' is 'there exists an x for which P(x) fails'.

questions.q: P(1) is true and P(k) implies P(k + 2) for all natural k. Then P(n) is certain for:
questions.explanation: From P(1) the step reaches P(3), P(5) and so on, so it covers all odd natural numbers.

questions.q: The roots of x² − 6x + 8 = 0 are:
questions.explanation: The equation factors as (x − 2)(x − 4) = 0, so the roots are 2 and 4.

questions.q: ∫ sec² x dx equals:
questions.explanation: The derivative of tan x is sec² x, so its antiderivative is tan x + C.

questions.q: The value of cos 20° cos 40° cos 80° is:
questions.explanation: Use cos θ cos(60° − θ) cos(60° + θ) = (1/4) cos 3θ with θ = 20°. This gives (1/4) cos 60° = 1/8.

questions.q: If a·b = 0 for two non-zero vectors a and b, the angle between them is:
questions.explanation: a·b = |a||b| cos θ = 0. Since the magnitudes are non-zero, cos θ = 0, so θ = 90°.

faq.q: What is a free JEE DPP mathematics sheet?
faq.a: It is a short daily set of mixed practice problems, usually eight to fifteen questions, that you attempt cold across every unit. The mix forces you to spot the topic before you solve.

faq.q: How many problems should I solve each day?
faq.a: Ten to twelve mixed problems a day is the sweet spot. It builds a recognition reflex, yet stays short enough that you never skip it.

faq.q: When should I start daily practice?
faq.a: As soon as you finish a unit's theory once. You do not need the whole syllabus first, so begin on the chapters you know and widen the mix over time.

faq.q: Where can I get ready-made mixed papers?
faq.a: The JEE Maths 30 Practice Papers e-book gives full mixed sets with worked solutions for Rs 79, an instant PDF you can print and drill from.
